references.text: Jericho and everything in the city were devoted to destruction (חֵרֶם) for the Lord, and all silver, gold, and articles of bronze and iron were to be holy to the Lord.
Achan took some of the devoted things, and the anger of the Lord burned against the people of Israel, showing the seriousness of breaking the ban.
Everything in Israel that is devoted to destruction shall belong to the priests, a parallel law concerning devoted goods.
It is forbidden to bring anything devoted into one's house, for then one oneself will be devoted to destruction.
A law regarding devoted goods from an idolatrous city: nothing of what was devoted should remain in anyone's hand.
Saul spared the best of what should have been devoted to destruction, and Samuel rebuked him for this.
All devoted goods in Israel shall belong to the priests, a restatement of the principle found in the messianic temple vision.
Whoever did not appear as commanded, all his property was to be devoted (יָחֳרַם), and he himself cast out.
A field that is devoted becomes holy to the Lord as devoted goods and belongs to the priest.
The continuation of the text explains further that people who are devoted cannot be redeemed.
